content: Moreover, when using a supervised approach, the “errors”, i.e. disagreement between the system output and human-provided labels, can point towards interesting cases for closer analysis and help us reflect on our conceptualizations. In the words of BIBREF2 , they can be “opportunities for interpretation”. Other types of “failures” can be insightful as well. Sometimes there is a “dog that didn't bark” BIBREF49 –i.e., something that everyone thinks we should have found, but we did not. Or, sometimes the failures are telling us about the existence of something in the data that nobody noticed, or thought important, until then (e.g., the large number of travel journals in Darwin's reading lists).
